newsitem.title: UK: Beckett to address utilities conference Monday - DTI.
newsitem.headline: Beckett to address utilities conference Monday - DTI.

text.p: Britain's trade secretary, Margaret Beckett, will address a London conference on regulation of the utilities industry at 0915 GMT on Monday, a spokesman for the department of Trade and industry said.
The speech will be one "of substance", he said and is to a conference in London organised by left leaning think tank the Institute for Public Policy Research.

But he refused to confirm or deny an article in The Sunday Times which said Beckett, the President of the Board of Trade, would use the speech to signal a shake-up of the system for regulating the utilities sector.
The article said the speech would mark the beginning of the end for high-profile regulators such as Clare Spottiswoode at Ofgas and Ian Byatt at water regulator Ofwat.
The Labour Party's manifesto for business said it would promote competition where possible and more effective regulation "where necessary."
It said it would also "consider the appointment of non-executive advisers to work with each regulator."

The Sunday Times said the government wanted to remove the cult of personality from utility regulation, replacing individual lead regulators with commissions consisting of three or more members in a bid to maintain tough control without public rows.

The Sunday Times article also said Beckett would use the speech to stress that the forthcoming windfall tax on privatised utility companies would be a one-off, never to be repeated. It quoted a government official as saying "The review will help us draw a line under the windfall tax."

It also suggested that the current price setting formulas, based on the level of retail prices minus a certain amount will also be re-examined. Instead a new system might be developed which aimed to share excess utility profits between consumers and shareholders, the paper said.
